The survey reads an interface a repository already has into its home: what the code and the rendered pages hold, measured where it can be, written as DESIGN.md and the interface rulings once the owner confirms it. Start it where the workspace names interface roots and holds no DESIGN.md, or when the owner asks for the interface's system to be written down.

## Choose the mode

Survey the repository whenever its source is at hand: only the source establishes token names and who owns them. Survey a site from its address alone only when no source exists; that needs a browser at a desktop and a phone width, samples up to three pages of different templates from the same site, and writes a draft labelled as reconstructed, since an address cannot show internal names or intent.

## Trace in order

Read, in this order: an existing DESIGN.md and any written guidance; the tokens, themes and global styles; the shared primitives and their variants; the representative pages; and the local styles last. A source counts only when the product imports it or renders it. Write a short hypothesis and what is out of scope before sampling, then sample representative surfaces and say what you left out.

## Measure with your own instrument

Write a small instrument into the project that measures what the sheet asks for, the distinct colours, faces, sizes, radii and spacing steps, and the routes, and declare it as one of the project's checks, so its numbers are recorded at a commit and anyone can run it again. Read the code and the rendered pages both; where they disagree, report both. Hierarchy and density need the rendered page.

## One row per fact

Each fact of the sheet is one row with one source: measured by a command at a commit, read by you from a file, or confirmed by the owner. A candidate value carries its role, its value, its source, its scope, how often it recurs and your confidence; promote a value when the computed and the declared values agree, or when it recurs across the samples.

## Confirm, then write

Put your hypotheses to the owner through cards where they render: the register at each root, the platform, the faces and colours that are the system and the ones that are accidents. Ask before writing where ownership is unclear, and once about any behaviour the product never had. Then write DESIGN.md from the smallest valid front matter, only the sections the evidence supports, in the format's order, its tokens taken only from named shared values, inventing no personality; and write the interface rulings. On an update, compare with the old file and keep every decision the owner accepted.

# Design survey: the practice's mechanics

This page holds where the survey's work lands and its commands. Read it with `SKILL.md` when the work lands in the workspace.

passages.gist: States where design-survey's work lands and its commands

passages.text:
## Where its work lands

- The sheet is `.greenline/ledger/interface/survey.json`, opening with its `generatedBy` key: one row per fact, `{ "fact", "value", "source" }`, the source one of `{ "kind": "measured", "command", "commit" }`, `{ "kind": "read", "from" }` or `{ "kind": "confirmed", "date" }`. `greenline check interface --survey` measures the rows it can and writes them, keeping every row you read and every row the owner confirmed.
- Your instrument is a script in the project, declared as a check with `greenline check --declare --name interface-survey -- <its command>` and run through `greenline check`, so its numbers are facts at a commit.
- DESIGN.md is written at the root, and at a root whose register differs; the rulings go under `## Interface` in `.greenline/DECISIONS.md`. Every write of the survey belongs to a change: where none is open, open a quick record first, and write the sheet, DESIGN.md and the rulings under it. The harness hook admits DESIGN.md and the ledger home before the owner's yes, never the decisions book.
- `.greenline/manifest.json`'s `interface` block holds the roots, the platform and the frameworks the setup detected: set `confirmed` to true once the owner confirms them. In the same round ask the owner once whether the interface check holds the close, the opt-in, and write the answer as `check`, `true` or `false`, never leaving it out; where it is true the check and the render hold `done` on every class, a platform no browser renders included.

## The section

Where a change is open, the record's `## start` section names `design-survey`, the mode, the sources read and the files it wrote, and cites the sheet. A survey with no change open opens a quick record first, its `## start` naming `design-survey`, and that change commits the sheet, DESIGN.md and the rulings.

## Commands

- `greenline status` prints the interface line and, once DESIGN.md reads, the drift between the code and it.
- `greenline check interface --survey` measures the sheet's rows at the current commit.
